title: Surge-aware canary stabilization plan and follow-ups after failed model rollout
creator: Avery Kim
description: Summary: During a staged canary rollout for model v23.4 we observed an unexpected latency surge and a user-facing tokenization regression routed through shadow traffic validation. The canary auto-rollback triggered after meeting the configured thresholds, but the incident exposed gaps in our surge-aware detection, canary window sizing, and post-rollback follow-up processes. This ticket captures the stabilization plan: runbook updates, signal refinements, A/B analysis artifacts, and concrete follow-up work for reliability and rollout tooling.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-08 09:10 UTC: Canary start (10% traffic). 2026-03-08 09:23 UTC: Latency increase flagged in synthetic SLO monitors. 2026-03-08 09:25 UTC: Shadow traffic telemetry showed tokenization mismatches. 2026-03-08 09:28 UTC: Auto-rollback executed per policy. 2026-03-08 09:35 UTC: Traffic normalized. 2026-03-08 10:00 UTC: Initial triage complete; rollback reason logged.
impact_summary: Temporary latency degradation for a subset of hosted API customers during the canary window; some requests experienced 2-3x tokenization variance causing downstream truncation for long prompts. No data exfiltration or security breach. Estimated affected traffic slice: ~7% of global requests during the window.
postmortem_summary: Root cause appears to be a model tokenizer mismatch combined with a spike in batch sizes from a misconfigured autoscaling policy in the dedicated pool used for canaries. The auto-rollback worked correctly, but our detection rules did not distinguish transient small spikes from model-induced semantic regressions. Observability gaps: missing per-token mismatch rate on canary dashboards and insufficient shadow traffic diffing tooling.
decisions: 1) Expand canary telemetry to include per-token mismatch rate and prefix-level KV cache hit ratios. 2) Add surge-aware smoothing to detection thresholds (short-term exponential backoff to avoid noisy rollbacks). 3) Tighten A/B comparison windows and add synthetic prompts focused on tokenization edge cases. 4) Schedule follow-up engineering tickets to harden autoscaling guards for canary targets.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook updated with explicit canary surge handling steps and human escalation path
New telemetry panels added: per-token mismatch rate, prefix KV cache hit, canary-batch-size distribution
Detection rules updated to include surge-aware smoothing and minimum evaluation window
A/B test harness extended with tokenization-focused prompt set and automated diffs
Post-change rollouts executed in shadow-only mode for two cycles without regression

runbook_updates: Add a dedicated section: 'Surge-aware Canary Handling' with steps to pause, increase evaluation window, and run synthetic tokenization probes
Define human escalation: on-call SRE -> runtime lead -> PM; include phone/SMS escalation if rollback threshold exceeded twice in 24h
Checklist for pre-rollout validation: tokenization parity check, KV cache warmup verification, autoscaler dry-run
rollback_rules: Maintain auto-rollback but require two independent signals before automated action: (latency or error spike) AND (semantic/tokenization mismatch > threshold)
Introduce minimum canary dwell time of 10 minutes unless explicit manual override
If autoscaler contributes >20% batch-size increase within 5m, treat as scaling noise and extend evaluation window

notes: Do not revert the decision to require dual-signal rollback. Emphasize observability-first fixes before relaxing dwell time. Coordinate with Support to notify customers who reported anomalies and offer an incident summary once final follow-ups complete.
